messages:
ajay: heads-up — seeing a sharp rise in preemptions in us-west2 over the last 45m, ~18% preempt rate on the preemptible pools. impact: a few 95th latency spikes and some request timeouts.
maria: ugh. is it a single AZ or across the region?
ajay: mostly AZ-b. other AZs look stable. cloud provider says maintenance + price pressure. infra-bot: ALERT: preempt_count(us-west2-AZb) = 127 in 1h; avg evict interval 27s.
sophie: can we soft-evacuate AZ-b and reshuffle workload to AZ-a/c before full spillover? prefer graceful instead of mass failover.
noah: soft-evac will need sticky-session handling for long-chat sessions and KV cache warmers. cold-starting KV will blow latency.
maria: proposal: tiered split during preempt surge
  - premium customers: prefer dedicated/reserved pools in other AZs/regions. route to quantized model variants only if reserved exhausted.
  - standard customers: aggressive fallthrough to regional best-effort and quantized variants; accept higher 95th.
ajay: +1. also want an emergency mode that favors latency SLOs for premium while shedding standard lower-priority traffic.
sophie: model-variant fallback idea: gptx-large -> gptx-large-8bit-quant (same weights, 8-bit), then -> gptx-medium for severe cases. keeps prompt semantics but cheaper and more available.
maria: need routing policy that encodes tier and preference order. sketch:
```
routing_policy:
  - match: customer.tier == "premium"
    prefer: [dedicated_pool, region_local_reserved_pool, other_region_reserved]
    fallback: [quantized_variant, per-request-degrade:soft]
  - match: customer.tier == "standard"
    prefer: [region_best_effort, mixed_spot_pool]
    fallback: [quantized_variant, other_region]
  global:
    preempt_threshold: 0.12 # start reshuffle above 12% preempt rate
    soft_drain_window: 90s
```
ajay: love it. question: how do we handle KV cache affinity? evict on node-level drains will invalidate a lot.
noah: options:
  - pre-warm caches in target pool during soft-drain (small window, background warming)
  - maintain per-session sticky routing key for 60s to avoid mid-request reroute
  - async cache-rebuild with stale-while-revalidate for 30s
sophie: we should also cap concurrency for standard customers when we hit soft_drain to keep premium latency stable.
maria: agree. and we can set autoscale buffer in other AZs: reserved + dynamic-burst (pay more) to absorb immediate load for premium.
ajay: cost tradeoff: paying for burst capacity vs degraded quality for standard. ops: run 2h post-mortem to tune thresholds.
infra-bot: ACTION: create incident ticket INF-2026-402 for us-west2 preempt surge; owners: @ajay @maria. ETA 15m.
noah: implementation notes: need a rollout plan for the routing changes — feature-flagged, start with canary 1% traffic (premium only), observe cache miss/latency.
sophie: also add fallback observability: per-customer fallback_count, fallback_reason, avg-latency-after-fallback.
ajay: I'll draft the canary plan and config. will include metrics to watch: preempt_rate, fallback_rate(premium|std), 95th latency, cache_miss_rate.
maria: if we want to be aggressive: add optional cross-region warm standby for top-20 customers during high churn windows. manual opt-in.
noah: one more gotcha: network egress costs if we move heavy traffic cross-region. need cost estimate before enabling warm-standby.
ajay: noted. i'll include cost delta in the plan. thanks all — i'll push a PR for the routing policy and the canary doc in ~30m. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — ping when PR is up.
infra-bot: NOTE: next auto-evac check in 5m.
